lines.text: Do you know how delivery companies plan their routes? A driver with a hundred stops has a puzzle no computer can solve perfectly.
Every extra stop multiplies the options. Just twenty five stops can be ordered in more ways than there are grains of sand on Earth.
So nobody checks every route. The software starts with a quick guess, like always driving to the nearest stop next.
Then it keeps swapping and flipping pieces of the route, and keeps every change that makes it shorter. Crossed paths untangle themselves.
Real systems also juggle traffic, delivery time windows, and how much each van can carry.
UPS even plans routes to avoid most left turns. Waiting to turn across traffic burns time and fuel, and it's riskier.
UPS says its routing system saves around a hundred million miles a year.
Orbi Work brings that idea to small teams. A task with coloured steps, and the files for each step wired right to it.
